notes:
This quest is a hub, not a ladder. Bullet 1 is a ZONE ENTRY -- Southern San d'Oria from East Ronfaure -- and there is no entity to click, so step 1 is a travel with a zone target and cannot carry a marker. The header names Cait Sith as the giver and gives no zone at all; the walkthrough never has you speak to anyone. Cait Sith is kept in start.npc because dropping it would leave the quest with no start NPC and no markable step, which validate treats as fatal and drops the quest entirely -- keeping it costs nothing (if no Cait Sith is standing there the marker simply never draws) and start.zone is set to the only zone the page names. Bullet 2 is the body of the quest: finish the three sibling quests the cutscene unlocks. They are separate quests with their own pages and markers, so there is nothing here to target -- one unmarkable rung that keeps the shape honest rather than three invented ones. NO evidence anywhere: 'Tiny memory fragment' and 'Large memory fragment' are both non-unique key-item names (several ids share each), so the resolver rejects them, and the Large fragment is the header's Reward besides, which rule 7 bars.

notes: A textbook ladder and one of the tidiest in this batch: two key items, both unique, both obtained exactly where the page says. Bullet 3 is two steps -- using the bait at the Claw Mark is the spawn, killing the NM is the fight -- so it splits and both rungs cite it. The Claw Mark is a real targetable entity (it folds to an npc key), so the spawn step keeps a marker; it is recorded as an object because that is what it is. The whole quest happens inside Ceizak Battlegrounds within one grid square of the bivouac: H-9 for Lucretia and the chapuli south of her, H-8 for the Claw Mark north of her. 'Fernfelling Chapulis' is written plural on the page and recorded singular, which is the entity name and not an invention. Mantid bait is step 2's evidence and step 3's requirement; Flayed mantid corpse is step 4's evidence and step 5's requirement -- neither is evidence twice. Both are key items (the corpse does not exist in the item table, only as key item 2220), so both are recorded as ki. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

notes: Demoted to medium for one reason, and it is not the ladder: the page says the quest only SHOWS IN YOUR LOG after bullet 4. The runtime treats accepting the quest as proof that step 1 is done, so for the first four bullets this quest is not started as far as the client is concerned and the ladder cannot run -- the player sees the Blandine start marker through a conversation, a second NPC, a return trip and a third NPC before stepping can begin. The reading itself is unambiguous, which is why nothing is flagged low. Bullet 3's 'exit the dock' is a positional instruction inside Mhaura, not a zone change -- the page names no second zone -- so it is a note on the second Blandine talk rather than a travel rung. The Sand Charm's source is a genuinely rare event -- Crossbones only appear on the Mhaura/Selbina ferry during a pirate attack -- so it rides the trade step as a drop role even though the ferry is a different zone from the step. Fame is blank with FLevel 4, which gates a level against no region.

notes: Bullets 3 and 4 are one step, not two: they are two conversations with Mulaujeant separated by a one Earth-minute wait, and only the second is observable (Sublime statue of the Goddess, key item 254). Two consecutive rungs on one NPC would be one marker anyway, so merging them loses nothing and puts the evidence where it is actually obtained. The wait is real-world minutes, not game time, and nothing reports it -- hence time_gated. The header's 'Quest Reqs' field is being used as an item manifest here (Elshimo Marble, Rauteinot's parcel, Sublime statue of the Goddess are the quest's own three objects), not as a gate, so it contributes nothing to gates. No obtain rung is invented for the marble: its Ivory Lizard source is a sub-bullet, and the trade step already carries it as a held requirement plus the mob as a drop role, so a Yuhtunga Jungle rung would add a position the player cannot be tracked through. Each key item is evidence exactly once and then a requirement on the next step, which is the shape the runtime reads best.

notes: Bullet 3 -- 'repeat this quest as often as you like' -- is the Repeatable header restated, not a step; a verb scan would have made a rung out of it. That leaves a talk and a trade on one NPC, which is one marker. The ladder is authored but will not actually be used for stepping, because this quest is repeatable and repeatable quests do not step: Rabbit Hide is a common stackable item, and holding some from a previous run would advance a fresh one. Worth knowing before anyone wonders why the rungs are quiet. The first-run-only detail is real and recorded on step 1 -- you must answer 'I shall help.' the first time and never again -- which is exactly why step 1 is not marked optional: it is required once, and the schema has no way to say 'the first time only'. Cletae at (D-8) upstairs in the Leathercraft guild is a vendor tip, not a step.
